summary: We created a website named beyond-the-space. It is a archive of all abandoned equipments in the surface of moon and Mars.
details: BEYOND THE MISSION Team AGNI-6 | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 Tagline: Some missions end. Their stories don't. 1. Project Overview Beyond the Mission is an interactive digital museum that documents and tells the stories of human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Throughout the history of space exploration, numerous machines, scientific instruments, landers, rovers, and mission components have been abandoned, deactivated, or intentionally left on planetary surfaces. These objects are more than discarded equipment. Each represents a scientific achievement, an engineering challenge, and an important chapter in humanity's exploration of space. Our project transforms these forgotten pieces of space history into an accessible, engaging, and educational digital storytelling experience. 2. Problem Statement Information about abandoned space exploration equipment is often scattered across technical documents, mission archives, and scientific databases. This makes it difficult for students, space enthusiasts, and the general public to discover the history and significance of these objects. People often have questions such as: - What equipment was left behind? - Which mission did it belong to? - What was its original purpose? - Why was it left there? - Where is it located? - What is its current status? Beyond the Mission aims to make these stories easier to discover, understand, and explore through a centralized digital platform. 3. Our Solution We developed a mobile-friendly interactive website that acts as a digital archive of abandoned and inactive space exploration equipment. Visitors can explore equipment records, discover mission histories, browse images, and understand the scientific importance of objects left behind on the Moon and Mars. By combining technology, historical information, and digital storytelling, our platform makes space exploration history more accessible to everyone. 4. Key Features 1. Moon and Mars Exploration Explore equipment records categorized by planetary location, allowing visitors to discover objects associated with lunar and Martian exploration. 2. Equipment Story Cards Discover individual objects through dedicated information cards containing their names, missions, original purposes, locations, and available status information. 3. Search and Filters Find specific equipment through search functionality and category-based filters. 4. Mission History Understand the historical background of space missions and the equipment associated with them. 5. NASA Imagery and Visual References Use space-related imagery to make the exploration experience more informative, engaging, and visually appealing. 6. Educational Experience Present complex space exploration information in a simple, accessible, and interactive format suitable for students and space enthusiasts. 5. Technology Stack and Development Tools - HTML5: Used to develop the structure and content of the website. - CSS3: Used for website styling, layouts, and responsive design. - JavaScript: Used to implement interactive features and website functionality. - GitHub: Used for source code management, repository creation, and version control. - Netlify: Used to deploy and host the website, making it publicly accessible through a live URL. - NASA Resources: Used for space-related information, research, and visual references. 6. Development and Deployment Workflow 1. Planned the project concept and identified the problem we wanted to address. 2. Designed and developed the website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. 3. Created a GitHub repository to store and manage the project's source code. 4. Connected the GitHub repository to Netlify. 5. Deployed the website using Netlify. 6. Made the project publicly accessible through its deployment URL. This workflow allowed us to develop, manage, and publish our prototype using accessible web development tools. 7. Target Audience - Students and educators. - Astronomy and space exploration enthusiasts. - Science communicators. - Researchers and science learners. - General public interested in space history and technology. 8. Expected Impact Beyond the Mission aims to: - Preserve the historical stories of space exploration equipment. - Increase public awareness of lunar and Martian missions. - Make space-related information easier to discover and understand. - Encourage students to explore science, engineering, and astronomy. - Transform forgotten mission hardware into an engaging educational experience. - Inspire curiosity about humanity's journey beyond Earth. 9. Future Scope The project can be expanded with additional features, including: - A larger database of abandoned and inactive space equipment. - Interactive maps showing the locations of equipment on the Moon and Mars. - Detailed mission timelines and historical records. - Integration with NASA APIs for updated imagery and mission information. - Three-dimensional visualizations of selected equipment. - More interactive educational content and exploration tools. These improvements could transform Beyond the Mission into a more comprehensive digital archive of humanity's space exploration legacy. 10. Team Information Team Name: AGNI-6 Team Size: 6 Members Competition: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 Project Title: Beyond the Mission Project Category: Space Exploration, Digital Storytelling, and Educational Technology 11. Our Vision Space exploration should not be remembered only through successful launches, famous astronauts, and historic landings. Every piece of equipment left behind represents a story of human curiosity, innovation, determination, and discovery. A rover that completed its journey, a lander that fulfilled its purpose, or an instrument that stopped transmitting data all remain part of humanity's exploration history. Through Beyond the Mission, we aim to preserve those stories and remind the world that even after a mission ends, its legacy continues. BEYOND THE MISSION Some missions end. Their stories don't. Developed with curiosity and innovation by Team AGNI-6.
